events.title: Eastern Market — Weekend Market & Flea
events.description: Historic public market plus weekend outdoor flea, arts, and crafts. Live music when weather permits.

events.title: Capitol Hill Farmers Markets
events.description: Seasonal weekend farmers markets with local produce and vendors.

events.title: Lincoln Park
events.description: Large Capitol Hill green space with playground, paths, and statues. Dog-friendly. Cafes at both ends.

events.title: Garfield Park
events.description: Neighborhood park with playground, tennis, basketball, bocce, and a community garden.

events.title: Yards Park & Navy Yard Waterfront
events.description: Riverfront park with fountains, boardwalk, and frequent seasonal weekend programming.

events.title: National Mall & Smithsonian Museums
events.description: Free Smithsonian museums and monuments. Reliable all-weather, all-ages option.

events.title: United States Botanic Garden
events.description: Free conservatory and gardens at the foot of the Capitol, with a Children's Garden.

events.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail Ride
events.description: Paved riverfront trail for a family bike ride, with Capital Bikeshare access nearby.

events.title: The Fields at RFK — Community Open Play & Disc Golf
events.time: Open hours vary (8 AM–dusk disc golf)
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus (401 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.description: Turf fields with community open-play hours plus DC's free disc golf course. 10-min walk from Stadium-Armory.

events.title: CHAW Gallery (Capitol Hill Arts Workshop)
events.venue: Capitol Hill Arts Workshop (545 7th St SE)
events.description: Rotating gallery shows of local artists, two blocks from Eastern Market. Check site for current exhibition.

events.title: Beetlejuice – The Musical (National Tour)
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington DC
events.description: The ghost with the most comes to DC in the acclaimed Broadway musical based on the classic Tim Burton film. A wildly funny, darkly quirky, and visually spectacular show.

events.title: Free Friday Concerts at Eastern Market Metro Park
events.venue: Eastern Market Metro Park, Capitol Hill
events.description: Every Friday in July starting July 3, free local music concerts are held at Eastern Market Metro Park. The series features diverse local DC acts — past performers include the DMV Music Academy steel pan ensemble and Moonscape (video game and anime soundtracks). Covers Fridays July 18 and July 25.

events.title: STC Academy Summer Repertory: Macbeth
events.venue: Shakespeare Theatre Company – Michael R. Klein Theatre, 450 7th St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets discounted vs. mainstage; under-35 pricing available. Likely ~$25–$55.
events.description: Shakespeare's propulsive tragedy, directed by Alec Wild with astonishing puppetry by Ksenya Litvak. Performed by the STC Academy Class of 2026 as part of their MFA repertory showcase — classical work in its purest form.

events.title: STC Academy Summer Repertory: Twelfth Night
events.venue: Shakespeare Theatre Company – Michael R. Klein Theatre, 450 7th St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets discounted vs. mainstage; under-35 pricing available. Likely ~$25–$55.
events.description: Directed by Jess Chayes, this is Shakespeare's most lyrical and enduring comedy — performed as the culmination of a year of classical training by the STC Academy Class of 2026. Runtime approximately 2 hrs 45 min with one intermission.

events.title: American Aspirations Exhibition at the Smithsonian Castle
events.description: The reopened Smithsonian Castle hosts 'American Aspirations,' an exhibition inviting visitors to consider how the founding ideals of 1776 have been interpreted and how each generation has reached toward new understandings of freedom, opportunity, and a shared future. Open daily through July 26 — catch it on the July 25–26 weekend.
events.source: Trust for the National Mall event calendar

events.title: District Fringe Festival – Closing Weekend
events.venue: Phoenix Theatre UDC / Firefly Amphitheatre, University of the District of Columbia
events.description: The homegrown District Fringe Festival closes out its run on its final weekend. The lineup features local performers in comedy, improv, storytelling, poetry, and Aye Aye: A Musical Pirate Adventure! Shows run both outdoors at Firefly Amphitheatre and indoors at Phoenix Theatre UDC.

events.title: Pippin
events.venue: Signature Theatre, 4200 Campbell Ave, Arlington, VA
events.price: Varies; Signature offers under-30 and rush pricing. Likely $35–$95.
events.description: Stephen Schwartz's (Godspell, Wicked) musical masterpiece of purpose, ambition, lust, and glory, thrillingly staged by director Matthew Gardiner for summer at Signature Theatre.

events.title: The Jury Experience at Miracle Theatre
events.description: Miracle Theatre on Capitol Hill presents The Jury Experience, described as a quirky and comedic live production running through July 26. Highlighted by Washingtonian as a top pick for the week of July 20–26.

events.title: What Became of Us
events.venue: Signature Theatre, 4200 Campbell Ave, Arlington, VA
events.price: Varies; Signature offers under-30 and rush pricing. Likely $35–$85.
events.description: A beautiful and moving play about two siblings striving for connection over the course of a lifetime — exploring memory, love, and what we leave behind.

events.title: Free Friday Concerts at Eastern Market Metro Park (July Series)
events.venue: Eastern Market Metro Park, Capitol Hill
events.description: Every Friday in July, free local music concerts are held at Eastern Market Metro Park. The series features a rotating lineup of local DC-area artists. July 25 weekend: Friday July 25 falls within this series. Performers include the DMV Music Academy steel pan ensemble and local ensembles playing video game and anime soundtracks.

events.title: Navy Yard Friday Night Concert Series (Summer Run)
events.description: The free Navy Yard Summer Concert Series returns to the Yards Park boardwalk every Friday, running June 12 through July 31. Come enjoy fantastic live bands, food and drinks, and river views along the Anacostia waterfront. Family-friendly with open grassy space for all ages. July 25 weekend: last confirmed Friday in-window is July 31.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series (14th Season)
events.description: The free Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series is back for its 14th season on the Yards Park boardwalk. Every Friday night this summer, come to Yards Park to enjoy the river view, fantastic bands, food and drinks, and restaurants within walking distance. Family-friendly with grassy open space. Covers Fridays July 18, July 25, and August 1.

events.title: Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.time: Various (4:00 PM, 6:00 PM, 8:00 PM Saturdays; 9:00 PM Fridays)
events.description: Washington Improv Theater's summer series 'Escape with Washington Improv Theater' runs July 11–August 1 at Studio Theatre (1501 14th St NW). Performances are confirmed on Saturday Aug 1 at 4:00 PM, 6:00 PM, and 8:00 PM, and Friday Jul 31 at 9:00 PM. WIT's shows are completely unscripted and driven by audience suggestions. First four weeks in the Milton Theater, second half in the Shargai space.

events.title: Mrs. Doubtfire (The Musical)
events.venue: Kennedy Center – Eisenhower Theater, 2700 F St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; KC Millennium Stage offers free daily performances separately. Tickets from ~$50+. MyTix rush available for ages 18–30.
events.description: The internationally acclaimed hit musical based on the beloved film. Everyone's favorite Scottish nanny comes to the Kennedy Center in this hilarious and heartfelt family-friendly comedy.

events.title: Mubadala DC Open – Weekend 1 (Opening Weekend)
events.time: Matches daily; schedule varies by session
events.venue: William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center, Rock Creek Park
events.description: The 57th edition of the only combined ATP/WTA 500 tournament in the world, running July 25–August 2. Hometown favorite Frances Tiafoe, Venus Williams, Naomi Osaka, Jessica Pegula, Taylor Fritz, Ben Shelton, and Alex de Minaur (defending champion) headline a stacked field. New outdoor fan zone, Michelin-starred food, and single-day VIP passes available. Spans all three target weekends.

events.title: Mubadala DC Open – Weekend 2
events.time: Matches daily; schedule varies by session
events.venue: William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center, Rock Creek Park
events.description: Finals weekend of the 2026 Mubadala DC Open — the only combined ATP/WTA 500 tournament in the world. Top seeds including Frances Tiafoe, Venus Williams, Naomi Osaka, Jessica Pegula, Taylor Fritz, and Ben Shelton compete for the title. New outdoor fan zone and Michelin-starred food on site. The tournament has sold out every session since 2019.

events.title: Art & Me Family Workshop: Outdoor Sculpture
events.venue: Freer Gallery of Art / Arthur M. Sackler Gallery (Asian Art Museum), National Mall
events.description: Recurring free Saturday family workshop where children ages 3–8 and their caregivers explore outdoor sculptures at the Smithsonian Asian Art Museum and learn how conservators preserve art exposed to the elements. Kids then make their own outdoor art to observe how it holds up, just like conservation experts do.

events.title: District Vibes / American Pride: How DC Changed American Culture
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library, 901 G St NW
events.description: A free exhibit exploring how DC shaped American culture — from inventing the football huddle and the modern blood bank to nurturing legends like Marvin Gaye. Discover vibrant contributions of Washingtonians through images, artifacts, storytelling and free programs. Main location at MLK Library with satellite locations across the city.

events.title: Lincoln Memorial Undercroft Museum
events.description: Newly opened free historical museum in a cavernous space beneath the Lincoln Memorial on the National Mall. One of two major new DC museums that opened in June 2026, offering a unique underground experience tied to one of America's most iconic monuments.

events.title: National Air and Space Museum – Reopened Final Galleries
events.venue: National Air and Space Museum, 600 Independence Ave SW
events.description: The National Air and Space Museum, celebrating its 50th anniversary, has just unveiled the final galleries in its years-long renovation project. A major milestone for one of the world's most visited museums — worth a fresh visit even for returning guests.

events.title: National Geographic Museum of Exploration
events.venue: National Geographic Museum of Exploration, Downtown DC
events.description: The brand-new National Geographic Museum of Exploration opened in June 2026, featuring massive sunny exhibit halls, immersive exhibits, and 'smart' screens throughout. A high-tech, visually rich experience for families and curious minds of all ages.

events.title: Smithsonian Dreams: Castle Façade Projection
events.description: On Friday and Saturday evenings, the façade of the Smithsonian Castle is illuminated with dynamic visuals inspired by the Smithsonian's extraordinary collections. A 20-minute digitized rotation featuring manuscripts, photos, and more. Free to view from the National Mall grounds.

events.title: Washington Nationals Baseball – Home Games at Nationals Park
events.venue: Nationals Park, 1500 S Capitol St SE
events.description: The Washington Nationals are in their home summer stretch at Nationals Park. The team — which has four NL East titles and a World Series championship — plays a full home schedule throughout July and August. Check the MLB schedule for specific game dates on target weekends.

events.title: CrazySexyCool – The TLC Musical
events.venue: Arena Stage (Kreeger Theater), 1101 6th St SW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets vary; TodayTix rush/lottery likely available
events.description: World premiere semi-biographical musical about TLC — Tionne, Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes, and Rozonda 'Chilli' Thomas — the most successful female group of all time. Charts their friendship, story, and legacy through their chart-topping music.

events.title: Something Rotten! (The Theatre Lab)
events.venue: Atlas Performing Arts Center, 1333 H St NE, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; The Theatre Lab productions typically ~$25–$50.
events.description: The Theatre Lab School of the Dramatic Arts stages this Tony-nominated musical comedy set in the Renaissance, where two brothers try to out-Shakespeare Shakespeare by writing the world's very first musical.

events.title: US Botanic Garden – Free General Admission & 'Fierce Flora' Exhibition
events.venue: United States Botanic Garden, Capitol Hill
events.description: The US Botanic Garden is free and open to the public on all target weekends. Explore the Conservatory's collections from arid deserts to tropical forests, view the 'Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise' exhibit, and see the ongoing 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' display. A beautiful, climate-controlled escape for families on hot summer days.

events.title: National Gallery of Art — Jazz in the Garden (Friday Evenings)
events.time: Fridays, evening (check nga.gov for exact times)
events.venue: National Gallery of Art Sculpture Garden
events.price: Free (food/drink available for purchase; alcohol requires 21+ ID)
events.description: The National Gallery of Art's beloved outdoor Friday-evening Jazz in the Garden concert series runs through August 14, 2026, with July performances on the 17th, 24th, and 31st. The concert takes place in the NGA Sculpture Garden on the National Mall. Admission is free; food and drinks are available for purchase (alcohol restricted to 21+, but families with teens are welcome to enjoy the garden atmosphere).

events.title: The Outsiders (The Musical)
events.venue: Kennedy Center – Opera House, 2700 F St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; MyTix rush available for ages 18–30.
events.description: Winner of four Tony Awards® including Best Musical. Adapted from S.E. Hinton's seminal novel and Francis Ford Coppola's iconic film, this thrilling production makes its highly anticipated Washington DC debut.

events.title: DPR Destination Movie Night Series at Yards Park
events.venue: Yards Park Great Lawn, Navy Yard
events.description: DC Department of Parks and Recreation hosts Destination Movie Night Series at Yards Park's Great Lawn every Thursday through August 20. Each night features themed activities at 6pm followed by a family movie at 7pm — themes include mask making with Bad Guys 2, a Pink Party for Barbie, and karaoke with Michael. A vibrant waterfront community movie experience.

events.title: The Fields at RFK Campus — Open Community Sports Complex
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus, 2400 East Capitol St NE
events.description: The Fields at RFK Campus — a 27-acre outdoor sports complex on the west bank of the Anacostia River — is open for community use through August 29, 2026. The multi-purpose complex features turf fields, bike paths, and a celebration pavilion. Open for permitted recreational play and community events all three target weekends. Note: RFK Stadium itself is under demolition and closed.

events.title: The Notebook – The Musical (National Tour)
events.time: Various (7:30 PM evenings; matinees Sat/Sun 2:00 PM)
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; avg ~$160–$230. TodayTix rush/lottery likely available.
events.description: Based on the best-selling Nicholas Sparks novel that inspired the iconic film, this moving musical tells the timeless love story of Noah and Allie across decades.

events.title: America 250 Scavenger Hunt at MLK Library
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library – Central Library
events.description: A drop-in scavenger hunt tied to America's 250th anniversary. Learn fun history facts around the library and win a prize. Available during all open hours on the target weekends.
events.source: DC Public Library – dclibrary.libnet.info (official events calendar)

events.title: Discover Summer at DC Public Library – Bingo, Activities & Reading Program
events.venue: All DC Public Library neighborhood branches
events.description: DC Public Library's all-ages, citywide celebration of reading and learning runs all summer. Pick up a Discover Summer Bingo Board at any neighborhood library or sign up online via Beanstack. Complete three tasks in a row to win prizes. This year's theme connects to America 250, inviting readers to imagine what America can become over the next 250 years.

events.title: MLK Jr. Memorial Library – Odyssey-Themed Stamp Rally
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library – Central Library, Great Hall
events.description: An ongoing self-guided Odyssey-themed stamp rally running all summer in the Great Hall of MLK Library. Drop in any open day during the target weekends to collect stamps and explore the library.
events.source: DC Public Library – dclibrary.libnet.info (official events calendar)

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Outdoor Market (Saturday)
events.description: Eastern Market's Saturday outdoor market runs July 4 through September 26 along 7th St SE, featuring local farmers, artists, crafters, and prepared food vendors from Pennsylvania Ave SE to North Carolina Ave SE. A 152-year-old community hub with live music, fresh produce, and handmade arts and crafts. Active on all three target weekends (July 26, Aug 1/2, Aug 8/9).

events.title: American Aspirations – Smithsonian Castle Special Exhibition
events.venue: Smithsonian Institution Building (The Castle), National Mall
events.description: Co-curated by Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch, American Aspirations brings together some of the Smithsonian's most treasured objects to commemorate the Declaration of Independence and examine how founding ideals have been interpreted across generations. Housed in the majestic Smithsonian Castle, temporarily open through September.

events.title: NMAH 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness' – America 250 Exhibition
events.venue: National Museum of American History, National Mall
events.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is leading the nation's 250th-anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition tracing how Americans have pursued the promises of the Declaration of Independence — life, liberty, and happiness. DC Public Library's Discover Summer program partners with NMAH for special weekend programming; check the library's table for activities and reading lists. Entry is free.
events.source: DC Public Library – dclibrary.org / Smithsonian NMAH

events.title: DC Improv Showcase Weekend – Benny Nwokeabia & Lineup
events.description: DC Improv weekend showcase featuring Benny Nwokeabia, Amber Hendrix, Tyler Horvath, Apple Brown Betty, and Matty Litwack. The Jul 24–26 run is confirmed on the official DC Improv Seat Engine calendar; Jul 18–19 falls within that same multi-night engagement. Showcases run ~90 minutes. 18+ with a 2-item food/drink minimum.

events.title: Girls Rock! DC July Summer Camp Showcase
events.description: Summer camp showcase from Girls Rock! DC featuring youth performers. A family-friendly, community-oriented afternoon concert event.

events.title: Right Round – 80s Alt Pop Dance Party
events.description: 80s alternative and pop dance party night at the Black Cat Red Room. Late-night bar event.

events.title: So Fetch – 2000s Dance Party
events.description: High-energy 2000s pop and alt dance party tribute act. A fun, accessible night for all ages at DC's legendary U Street club.

events.title: Rock the Dock: The Fearless Eras (Taylor Swift Tribute)
events.description: Free Friday night concert on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier featuring The Fearless Eras, a Taylor Swift tribute band. Part of the all-summer Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. Genres include pop and country. Bring a blanket or chair; food available from Wharf restaurants and the stageside kiosk.

events.title: Free Screening: Summer Season of Anime 2026
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library – Central Library
events.description: Free anime screening at MLK Library, shown on a projector and open to all. Part of DC Public Library's summer programming calendar for teens and families.

events.title: Hill Family Biking: Yards Park Ride
events.venue: Watkins Elementary School (Parking Lot on D St SE)
events.description: A 4-mile family bike ride from Capitol Hill to Yards Park to cool off with free ice cream and fun at the pool. Volunteers marshal to keep the group together; MPD bike team participates. Bring your bike — basic mechanic help available 15 minutes before start.

events.title: Holy Rollers with Hammered Hulls and The Owners
events.description: Punk/rock showcase headlined by DC legends Holy Rollers, with Hammered Hulls and The Owners supporting. A classic underground DC rock night.

events.title: Jackie Kashian at DC Comedy Loft
events.description: Stand-up comedian Jackie Kashian performs at the DC Comedy Loft (1523 22nd St NW). Shows confirmed for July 23–25 on multiple aggregator calendars. Two-item minimum per person in the showroom.

events.title: Poet Life Fest at Gateway DC Pavilion
events.description: A free poetry festival at Gateway DC Pavilion in Congress Heights. Calling all poets and poetry lovers for a Saturday celebration of spoken word and local literary arts.

events.title: Rahill
events.description: Rahill (of Jhené Aiko's background) performs solo at the 9:30 Club. Indie R&B and ethereal vocals in an intimate club setting.

events.title: Rhizome Fashion Festival
events.description: An offbeat annual fashion festival featuring local bands modeling clothing from local designers — including Lost Destination, known for 'over-embellished gothic costumes.' The event includes live music, workshops, a clothing swap, a photoshoot, and blind contour drawings. Located in Takoma DC.

events.title: Sheryl Underwood at DC Improv
events.description: Emmy-award-winning comedian and co-host of 'The Talk' Sheryl Underwood headlines at DC Improv. Multiple shows confirmed across the Jul 24–26 weekend on aggregator and washington.org listings. 18+ with a 2-item food/drink minimum.

events.title: Smithsonian Family Day: America's 250th Birthday Celebration
events.description: The Smithsonian welcomes families and kids of all ages to celebrate America's 250th birthday. Free, daylong event featuring immersive activity zones, theater performances by Discovery Theater, a Washington Ballet movement class, PBS KIDS characters, historical reenactors, a community mural project, live jazz in the Enid A. Haupt Garden, and garden planting activities. No tickets or advance registration required.

events.title: Taylor Williamson at Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse
events.description: Comedian Taylor Williamson performs at Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse (2903 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA). Multiple shows confirmed for Jul 24–26 weekend on aggregator listings. Tickets typically $18–$28 per the venue's stated price range. 21+ unless accompanied by a parent.

events.title: Tour de Francs – C3 Chesapeake Cycling Club (via WABA)
events.venue: Ridgely, MD (start location TBD on registration)
events.description: A no-cost 26-mile community ride hosted by C3 Chesapeake Cycling Club and listed on WABA's events calendar. Features a strawberry shortcake pit stop along the route, followed by a hotdog and BBQ celebration at the finish. Ride at your own pace with food and support throughout.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at The Wharf: Apollo 13 (Free Outdoor Movie)
events.description: Free outdoor screening of Apollo 13 (1995) on the Transit Pier's large LED screen, presented by Pacifico Beer. Part of the Wharf's weekly Wednesday Sunset Cinema series — this is the Wednesday evening event closest to the July 25 weekend. Limited Adirondack chairs available first-come, first-served. Food available from Wharf restaurants.

events.title: Rock the Dock: 7 Deadlies (Rock / Pop Covers)
events.description: Free Friday night concert on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier featuring 7 Deadlies, a pop and rock cover band. Part of the Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. Seating is limited; food and drinks available from Wharf restaurants.

events.title: Rock the Dock: 7 Deadlies (Rock)
events.description: 7 Deadlies, a pop and cover rock band, performs on the Floating Stage on Transit Pier as part of The Wharf's free Friday night Rock the Dock summer concert series, presented by Pacifico Beer.

events.title: Souls of Mischief
events.description: Oakland hip-hop legends Souls of Mischief perform at Union Stage. Known for classic 90s rap including '93 'Til Infinity.

events.title: ALL THE FEELINGS TOUR: Metric, Broken Social Scene & Stars
events.description: A landmark Canadian indie-rock triple bill: Metric, Broken Social Scene and Stars co-headline the All The Feelings Tour at The Anthem.

events.title: Lincoln Theatre – Saturday Night Show (Aug 1)
events.description: Live music at the historic Lincoln Theatre on U Street. Artist TBA — confirmed show slot with GA standing ($15.50) and balcony seats ($28.25) on sale.

events.title: Max Meisel at DC Comedy Loft – Cellar Loft Debut
events.description: Max Meisel makes his Cellar Loft Debut at the DC Comedy Loft. Meisel is an LA-based comedian currently featuring on Tom Arnold's 'My Crazy X-Wife' tour, and producer of BackDoor Comedy. Run confirmed for July 31–August 1 on the official DC Comedy Loft events page. Two-item minimum per person.

events.title: RenRiot and Gina Young
events.description: RenRiot and Gina Young perform at the Black Cat. Independent and alternative artists on DC's storied U Street corridor.

events.title: United We Dance
events.description: Dance music showcase at the 9:30 Club. Electronic and dance-oriented acts in DC's most iconic mid-size venue.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at The Wharf: Roman Holiday (Free Outdoor Movie)
events.description: Free outdoor screening of Roman Holiday (1953) on the Transit Pier's large LED screen, presented by Pacifico Beer. Part of the weekly Wednesday Sunset Cinema series — this is the Wednesday closest to the Aug 1 weekend. All ages welcome; dogs on leash welcome.

events.title: DC Punk Archive 2026 Summer Rooftop Shows – August
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library – Rooftop / 5th Floor Event Space
events.description: The 12th season of the legendary DC Punk Archive Rooftop Shows at MLK Library continues with a second summer show (scheduled for August, first Wednesday of the month). Free, all ages, rain or shine (rain location: 5th floor Event Space). Local D.C.-area bands perform on the rooftop garden overlooking the city. Presented by Mount Pleasant and MLK Library Friends. Outside food and non-alcoholic beverages welcome.
events.source: DC Public Library – dclibrary.libnet.info (official events calendar)

events.title: Rock the Dock: Salsa Dance Night ft. Salsa with Silvia & Cubano Groove
events.description: Free themed salsa dance night on the pier featuring instructor Salsa with Silvia and live music by Cubano Groove, part of the Rock the Dock Friday night concert series. Each dance night features a different style of music and dancing al fresco on Transit Pier.

events.title: Rock the Dock: Salsa Dance Night with Cubano Groove
events.description: Free Friday themed dance night on Transit Pier combining live salsa music by Cubano Groove with instruction by Salsa with Silvia. Part of the Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. One of several themed dance nights on select Fridays this summer where each night features a different style of music and dancing.

events.title: Chesapeake DockDogs Competition at The Wharf
events.description: A full day of high-flying, tail-wagging action as Chesapeake DockDogs brings their nationally sanctioned DockDogs dog-jumping competition to District Pier. Watch dogs leap for distance and height into the water in this all-ages spectator-friendly waterfront event.

events.title: Discover Summer at Lincoln's Cottage – Outdoor Family Festival
events.venue: President Lincoln's Cottage, Rock Creek Church Rd NW
events.description: DC Public Library celebrates Discover Summer with a family festival on Abraham Lincoln's historic lawn at Lincoln's Cottage. Features crafts, games, and community activities on the 250-acre campus. A historic site and museum with experiences for all ages. DC Library staff will be present with reading lists, activities, and library swag.

events.title: KALEO – Way Down We Go Tour (with Dogpark)
events.description: Icelandic blues-rock powerhouse KALEO brings their Way Down We Go Tour to The Anthem, with indie-rock opener Dogpark.

events.title: Lincoln Theatre – Saturday Night Show (Aug 8)
events.description: Confirmed show slot at Lincoln Theatre on August 8. Artist TBA — doors 7:30 PM, show 8:30 PM. Check the official site for lineup updates.

events.title: National Zoo Elephant Day – DC Library Storytimes & Giveaways
events.description: National Zoo Elephant Day celebrates Asian elephants and the Smithsonian's long-standing commitment to their care and conservation. DC Public Library librarians will be on-site hosting special storytimes, giving away library swag, and sharing reading recommendations as part of the Discover Summer partnership. The Zoo itself is free to enter.

events.title: Tommy Davidson at DC Improv
events.description: Tommy Davidson, known for countless unforgettable sketches on 'In Living Color,' headlines at DC Improv. Confirmed as an 'early August' engagement by dc-improv.ticketsfairfax.net and listed among the DC Improv's Jun–Dec 2026 headliner slate on washington.org. 18+ with 2-item minimum.

events.title: MLK Library Rooftop Punk Shows — Season 12 (August Date: Abacot, Girls on Toast + Guest)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Rooftop
events.description: The MLK Library's legendary all-ages rooftop concert series returns for its 12th season, marking 50 years of punk in the United States. The August 12 show features Abacot, Girls on Toast, and a to-be-announced special guest. All performances are free and open to all ages — described as 'the most fun you will ever have at the library.' The first show of the season was July 8.

events.title: Sunset Cinema at The Wharf: 10 Things I Hate About You (Free Outdoor Movie)
events.description: Free outdoor screening of 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) on the Transit Pier's large LED screen, presented by Pacifico Beer. Part of the weekly Wednesday Sunset Cinema series — this is the Wednesday closest to the Aug 8 weekend. All ages welcome; dogs on leash welcome.

events.title: Argo and the Violet Queens with Massie, Cuni & Pink-house
events.description: Argo and the Violet Queens headline with supporting acts Massie, Cuni, and Pink-house. Independent and alternative music at Black Cat.

events.title: Howard Jones: Things Can Only Get Better Tour (with Wang Chung, The English Beat, Modern English & more)
events.description: A massive 80s new wave extravaganza featuring Howard Jones, Wang Chung, The English Beat, and Modern English. Multiple confirmed headliners on one bill.

events.title: Oh He Dead
events.description: Oh He Dead performs at the 9:30 Club. Genre-bending live act at DC's premier U Street concert club.
